subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps

Hi Samira (and Jorge),

Great to chat this morning - thanks for walking through your recommendation engine use case and the specific quality pain points around entity hallucination and sensitive-field handling. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move to a short evaluation: 

What we heard
- Primary goal: surface high-precision product suggestions in checkout flows while avoiding any PII leakage.
- Typical input: short customer messages (1-3 sentences), sometimes with order numbers or addresses.
- Edge cases: malformed addresses, ambiguous product synonyms, and truncated chat history.

Proposed evaluation plan
1) Model shortlist: run a lightweight benchmark on 3 candidate models (small/medium/large):
   - redwood-mini-7b-v2 (fast, lower cost)
   - open-llama-13b-chat-q4 (balanced quality/cost)
   - redwood-4o-15b (higher quality for higher-risk flows)
2) Prompt set: collect ~20 representative prompts (we've attached a template) including 5 labeled edge cases and 3 expected-output examples per prompt.
3) Security: please confirm whether prompts will include raw PII or whether you prefer redacted versions - we can accept raw prompts via our secure upload link (below) or you can send redacted examples.
4) Timeline: if we get prompts by EOD Thu (2026-09-03), we can deliver benchmark results within 5 business days.

Attachments: prompt_collection_template.csv (template for prompts), benchmark_summary_acme.pdf (baseline summary from similar retailers)

Next steps for you
- Fill top 20 prompts into the template (real examples are preferred).
- Mark any prompts that are high-risk (contains emails, phone numbers, order ids).
- Upload to: https://redwood.uploads/secure/acme-prompt-upload?id=9f8e7d

I'll loop Rishi and Neha for redaction and security guidance on accepted formats. Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if that helps - what times work for you on Thursday?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa - this plan looks good. A couple quick questions before we gather the prompts:

1) For PII: we'd prefer to avoid sending raw customer emails or full order IDs where possible. Is it OK to use canonical redaction tokens (e.g., <EMAIL>, <ORDER_ID>)? If you need the raw text to evaluate extraction accuracy, can we use a secure link instead?

2) Regarding the model shortlist: curious if the redwood-4o-15b is required for production or mainly for boundary testing? Also, any cost guidance for running the 3-model benchmark?

3) Will the benchmark include prompt-level metrics (precision/recall for entity extraction) or just generation quality metrics?

We can aim for the EOD Thu deadline but I may need to pull some prompts from our CS team so might be close. Appreciate confirmation on the redaction approach and any upload instructions.

- Samira

ACME Inc.

Hi Samira - short answers here and some extra context: 

PII / redaction
- Using canonical tokens like <EMAIL>, <ORDER_ID>, <PERSON>, <NUM> is perfectly fine for an initial functional benchmark. For extraction/NER-specific metrics, raw or minimally masked data is more accurate, but we understand constraints.
- Secure upload: use this link (TLS + customer-specific encryption at rest): https://redwood.uploads/secure/acme-prompt-upload?id=9f8e7d. Files are scoped to the ACME account and auto-deleted from the upload staging area after 30 days unless you request otherwise.

Model guidance & cost
- redwood-mini-7b-v2: fastest and cheapest - good for latency-sensitive paths.
- open-llama-13b-chat-q4: balanced choice; we typically recommend this for mid-tier accuracy at reasonable cost.
- redwood-4o-15b: reserved for higher-risk flows where hallucination tolerance must be minimal; treat it as the "high-quality" baseline.
- Cost estimate for the 3-model run (20 prompts x ~3 completions each): ~$150-$300 total (depends on sequence length). We'll confirm exact numbers when we receive the prompt CSV.

Evaluation metrics we will provide
- Per-prompt: generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE-style where applicable), semantic similarity to expected outputs, and a targeted entity-precision/recall check for labeled prompts.
- Aggregate: latency, cost per token, and example failure cases with recommended prompt tweaks.

Attached a short example prompt_set_examples.csv to show how to label edge cases + expected outputs. If you can flag 3-5 "pass/fail" acceptance criteria per prompt (e.g., "must not hallucinate price"), that will help our regression checks.

Timing: Thu EOD works - if you hit any delays, ping me and we'll adjust the run.

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps

Looping in a quick redaction checklist for acme's team to make ingestion smooth:

Redaction checklist (recommended)
- Replace personal names and emails with <PERSON> / <EMAIL>.
- Replace order numbers / invoice ids with <ORDER_ID> and numeric sequences with <NUM>.
- Leave product SKUs as-is if they are important for model signals; if SKU contains PII-like sequences, replace and note mapping in a separate file.
- For addresses: keep city/state; redact street numbers to <NUM_ADDR> where necessary.
- Mark any prompts that include financial amounts or discounts with a TAG_FINANCIAL label in the CSV.

Internal note: once they upload, I can run a quick sanity check for obvious PII and a small data-quality pass (15-30 min) and return a cleaned file we can feed to the benchmark. Happy to help with labeling guidance if their CS team is short on time.

- Neha
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
